claim: SAE-derived code-correctness directions in base Gemma-2-2b detect incorrect code with F1=0.821 but correct-predicting features reach only F1=0.504.
stance_target: hidden states carry asymmetric code correctness signal (L2)
quoted_support: detection directions predict errors reliably (F1: 0.821) but fail as confidence indicators for correct code (F1: 0.504), revealing asymmetry in how models represent code correctness.

breadth.confidence_families: SAE feature activations as predictors (t-statistic selected); no verbal or sampled confidence
breadth.base_vs_instruct: yes: base directions tested on instruction-tuned model (Sec 5.5)
breadth.elicitation_formats: single standardized MBPP prompt with code initiator (Figure 1)
breadth.label_source: pass@1 on 3 MBPP test cases at temperature 0 (Sec 4)
breadth.label_independence: data split 50% direction selection, 10% threshold and coefficient calibration, 40% mechanistic analysis (Sec 4)
breadth.calibration_metrics: F1 and AUROC (Sec 5.1); no ECE or Brier
breadth.granularity: whole-solution (activation at final prompt token before generation)
breadth.causal_intervention: yes: steering, attention analysis, weight orthogonalization (Sec 5.2-5.4)

claim: Steering with correctness directions fixes 4.04% of errors but corrupts 14.66% of correct code; orthogonalizing correct directions causes 83.62% corruption vs 18.97% for control.
stance_target: causal intervention on code-correctness directions is occupied
quoted_support: fixing 4.04% of errors but corrupting 14.66% of correct code, necessitating selective rather than universal application.

claim: Directions from the base model retain effectiveness after instruction tuning: F1=0.821 base vs F1=0.772 instruct, with MBPP pass rate rising from 29.9% to 38.4%.
stance_target: base-to-instruct persistence of code-correctness signal (L2 base/instruct pairs)
quoted_support: The incorrect-preferring feature (L19-5441) achieves F1=0.821 in the base model and F1=0.772 after instruction-tuning.
